subject: bigfin squid
title: This Squid Can Be 8 Meters Long. No One Has Ever Caught an Adult

scenes.text: This squid can be eight metres long. Nobody has ever caught one.
The bigfin squid has been filmed only about a dozen times in thirty years, mostly by deep-sea robots.
Its body is small. Its arms are up to twenty times longer, thin as spaghetti.
And it holds them out sideways, then bends them straight down, like elbows.
Scientists think the kink may stop those endless arms from tangling.
It's been seen over six kilometres deep. It's out there. We just can't reach it.

description:
The bigfin squid's arms and tentacles may reach 8 metres or more, up to 15 to 20 times its mantle length, held out at strange 'elbows'.
It has been filmed only around a dozen times in 30 years, and not a single adult has ever been captured.
What do you think it eats with arms like that?
first_comment: The first adult was spotted from a submarine in 1988, off Brazil, almost 5 kilometres down. What deep-sea animal should we cover next?
